info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

get.description: The caller's offers still open, soonest to expire first (at most 50).

post.description:
The caller takes the queue item offered to them: it is picked for them,
and a service ticket it holds with no assignee is assigned to them.
Audited.

404.description: No such offer to the caller

409.description: The offer expired or was decided, or the item was taken

post.description:
The caller refuses the queue item offered to them; it is offered to the
next available agent. Audited.

404.description: No such offer to the caller

409.description: The offer expired or was decided

post.description: Assigns one ticket already in the queue by the queue's distribution strategy. Audited.

404.description: No such queue, or the ticket isn't in this queue

409.description: Ticket already assigned, queue inactive, another claim/assign is in progress, or no member has capacity

422.description: assignee_id required/forbidden for this queue's distribution, or names a non-member

post.summary: Claim the next ticket in a queue
post.description: The caller takes the queue's next waiting ticket. Audited.

200.description: Success (claimed may be false if the queue has nothing open)

403.description: Caller is not an active member or lead of this queue

409.description: Queue is not active, another claim is in progress, or the caller is at capacity

get.description: The active service offerings, searched in Arabic or English across name, description and category.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words to look for in the name, description and category.

parameters.name: category_ref
parameters.description: Only offerings in this catalog category.

get.description: The catalogue offerings a requester can pick from.

post.description: Creates a work request that takes the offering's defaults (priority, SLA policy, queue). Audited.

post.summary: Publishes an offering as its next version (G3-T1).
post.description:
The offering becomes public, and a snapshot of it is kept as a numbered
`service_offering_version`, so what a request was filed against stays
known after the offering changes.

409.description: The offering is being published already, or changed meanwhile

post.description:
One work request with one item per line (and per offering of an order
guide, each carrying the guide's answers). An item whose offering
requires approval waits for it; the others start their fulfilment tasks
at once.

404.description: The first line's offering is not active

422.description: No lines or too many, a bad quantity, or an unanswered guide question

post.description:
Allowed while it waits for approval or is being fulfilled; its open and
pending tasks are cancelled with it. Only the person the order is for, the
one who placed it, or an administrator may; anyone else gets 404.

404.description: No such item, or not one the caller may cancel

409.description: The item is fulfilled, rejected or cancelled already

get.description: The caller's service orders and where each item stands.

post.description:
Ghost assignments that respect the hard rules and keep travel low; the
proposal is never committed.

x-audit-exempt.note: computes a proposal and writes nothing; the dispatcher assigns what they accept

post.summary: Records readings posted by devices that know only their own id.
post.description:
Each reading names `device_id`; the asset holding that device id is
looked up and the reading is created on it through the generic write
path. A reading of an unknown device, or one that fails validation, is
answered with its error and does not stop the others. Device rules see
the readings on the next device readings run.

get.description: The hand-offs waiting for the caller: to them, or to a queue they are a member of.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

200.description: Hand-offs waiting for the caller or their queues

post.description: Takes the handed-off work, with the hand-off's `If-Match` row version. Audited.

200.description: Accepted; the ticket is the caller's

403.description: Not handed to the caller or a queue of theirs

409.description: No longer waiting, a stale row_version, or another hand-off in progress

post.description: Gives the work back with a note, with the hand-off's `If-Match` row version. Audited.

403.description: The caller is not the ticket's assignee

409.description: Already closed, a stale row_version, or another hand-off in progress

422.description: If-Match missing or malformed, no note, or not an agent's hand-off

get.description:
Each record the mailbox's messages were routed to, with the message
count and the latest message's time, latest first.

200.description: The mailbox's conversations, latest message first

get.description:
The active shared mailboxes (mailbox integration systems), by name, all
on one page.

200.description: The active shared mailboxes, by name

post.summary: Runs the disposition of every inspected return line.
post.description:
A refund makes a draft credit note on the line's invoice line, a
restock a return stock movement into the return's restock location,
and a replace a draft replacement order; repair, scrap and return to
vendor are recorded. Each line acts once: a repeat answers
`already_done` with what the line made.

404.description: No such return, or returns are not installed

409.description: The return is not received or inspected yet

post.description:
An append-only movement and the balance it changes, in one transaction under the balance row's
lock, so the balance is always the sum of its movements. Audited.

201.description: The movement and the balance after it

409.description: The same stock is being created by another request; retry

422.description: Not enough stock, or an unknown kind or quantity

post.description:
Holds a quantity of a product at a location for a reference, until it is released or expires.
Audited.

409.description: The same stock is being created by another request; retry

post.description: The held quantity is free again. Audited.

204.description: Released; its stock is available again

409.description: The reservation is not held

post.description: A person hands the ticket to another person or a queue, with a summary of where it stands. Audited.

404.description: No such ticket the caller can see

409.description: A hand-off of this ticket is already waiting or in progress

422.description: No summary or reasoning, or a target the caller cannot see

get.description: Every hand-off of the ticket, between agents and people, with its outcome.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

404.description: No such ticket the caller can see

post.summary: Declares a major incident on a ticket.
post.description:
Sets the commander, pages whoever is on call on the chosen schedule and
the commander, opens a bridge on the video provider named, and posts a
status page incident. Declaring again answers the first declaration.

404.description: No such ticket, or ITSM is not installed

409.description: Someone else is declaring it

post.summary: Links tickets to a major incident.
post.description:
Each ticket gets the major incident as its parent; a ticket already
linked is answered as linked.

409.description: Not declared as a major incident

post.description:
Records the restore time on the ticket, resolves its status page
incident and posts the last update to subscribers.

409.description: Not declared as a major incident

post.summary: Say I am viewing a record, and see who else is.
post.description:
Records the caller's heartbeat on a record they can read (kept two
minutes) and answers the other people viewing it now, most recent first.
Send it every `heartbeat_secs` while the record is open.

200.description: Who else is viewing the record

404.description: No such record, or the caller cannot read it

x-audit-exempt.note: a viewing heartbeat kept two minutes in Redis; no business or security effect

post.description:
With `confirm: true`, queues the job that writes each asset's warranty expiry date through the
record engine as the person who confirmed, 500 assets a batch. Audited.

Counts the assets whose warranty expiry date would change from their active warranty entitlements,
and shows a few. Writes nothing.

x-audit-exempt.note: counts the assets the backfill would change; writes nothing

get.summary: Ranks the technicians who can take a work order.
get.description:
Technicians pass the hard rules (skills, territory, hours and van
parts) and are ordered on-time first, then by travel estimate and SLA
slack. Nothing is assigned: the dispatcher picks.

parameters.name: include_without_parts
parameters.description: Also answer technicians whose van lacks parts (default false).

404.description: No such work order, or field service is not installed

get.description:
The overall status, each public component, the open incidents and the planned maintenance, rebuilt
at most every 30 seconds. No session.

404.description: The service module is not licensed

get.description: The confirmation page for an emailed link; its button confirms. No session.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The signed token from the link.

200.description: A page with a confirm button

post.description: Confirms the subscription the token names. No session.
Asks to receive status updates by email; a confirmation link is sent. No session.

202.description: A confirmation is on its way (the same answer for any address)

404.description: The service module is not licensed

get.description: The unsubscribe page for an emailed link; its button unsubscribes. No session.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The signed token from the link.

200.description: A page with an unsubscribe button

post.description: Stops the subscriber's emails. No session.

get.summary: The survey page a signed link opens.
get.description:
A plain bilingual form that posts its answers; a link that is invalid,
expired or answered shows a page saying so.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The signed token from the email.

200.description: The survey as a form page, or a page saying the link is no longer valid

post.summary: Stores the answers a survey page posts, once.
post.description: The same checks as the JSON route; the answer is a page, not JSON.

200.description: A page thanking the respondent, or saying what is wrong

get.summary: The survey a signed link opens.
get.description:
No sign-in: the link is the credential. A link that was answered, has
expired or was tampered with answers the same 404.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The signed token from the email.

404.description: The link is not valid, has expired or was answered

post.summary: Stores the answers of a signed link, once.
post.description:
Each answer is checked against its question; the response is written
only while it is unanswered, so one link answers one response.

404.description: The link is not valid, has expired or was answered

422.description: An answer does not fit its question

post.description:
The same recalculation for up to 500 tickets after `after`, in id order; call again with
`next_after` until it is `null`. Each ticket commits on its own. Automation administrators only.
Audited.

200.description: One page of unresolved SLAs recalculated

post.summary: Apply an SLA policy to a ticket
post.description:
Assigns the SLA policy that matches the ticket and computes its resolution deadline in business
time, or records why it could not. Needs update rights on tickets. Audited.

204.description: No matching or fallback SLA policy is configured

post.description:
Stops the ticket's SLA time from counting until it is resumed; a second pause or resume already
in progress is 409. Needs update rights on tickets. Audited.

409.description: Another pause/resume request for this ticket is already in progress

post.description:
Starts the clock again now and recalculates the deadline from the time left. Needs update rights
on tickets. Audited.

409.description: Another pause/resume request for this ticket is already in progress

post.description:
For a ticket whose SLA deadline could not be worked out (its business calendar did not resolve),
tries again: stores the deadline when it resolves now, or records another attempt. Any other
ticket is left alone, so it is safe to repeat. Needs update rights on tickets. Audited.

200.description: The ticket's SLA state after recalculation (unchanged unless it was unresolved)

409.description: A pause/resume request for this ticket is in progress

get.description:
The ticket's audit events, status changes, communications and linked decisions in one feed, newest
first, filtered to what the caller may read. Anyone who may read tickets.

404.description: No such ticket, or the caller cannot see it

post.summary: Converts a work request with conversion maps (G2-T3).
post.description:
Each map creates one record of its entity from the request's fields; more
than one map splits the request into several records, created together.

409.description: Already converted or rejected

422.description: A map is not active or not valid, or a target record failed validation

post.summary: Convert a work request to a project
post.description:
Creates a project from the work request and marks the request converted, in one transaction. Needs
the right to create projects and to update the request. Audited.

409.description: Already converted or rejected

422.description: organization_id does not name a live organization

post.summary: Convert a work request to a task
post.description:
Creates a task from the work request and marks the request converted, in one transaction. Needs the
right to create tasks and to update the request. Audited.

409.description: Already converted or rejected

422.description: project_id does not name a live project

post.summary: Convert a work request to a ticket
post.description:
Creates a service ticket from the work request and marks the request converted, in one transaction.
Needs the right to create tickets and to update the request. Audited.

409.description: Already converted or rejected

422.description: The ticket failed validation (e.g. the request has no requester)

ActorKind.description: B1-T1: who made a timeline entry.

resolution_due_at.description: The calculated deadline; `null` when the SLA is unresolved.

oneOf.description: Why no deadline could be calculated; `null` when it was.

assignee_id.description:
Required when the queue's distribution is `manual`; optional for
`skill_match` (the member must hold the skills); must be omitted for
`round_robin`/`least_loaded`, whose target is computed automatically.

slack_minutes.description:
Minutes between arrival (now plus travel) and the job's due time;
negative when late.

travel_minutes.description: Minutes to the site, when both points are known.

claimed.description:
`false` when the queue is currently empty — not an error, just
nothing to claim right now.

organization_id.description:
The organization the new project is created under — required because
`organization_id` is a required lookup on `attome_project` and nothing on
`service_work_request` names one.

project_id.description:
The project the new task (`project_work_item`) is created under —
required because `project_id` is a required lookup on that entity and
nothing on `service_work_request` names one.

map_ids.description: The maps to convert with, in order; more than one splits the request.

values.description:
Values for the target records that the request cannot supply (a
required parent, say), applied over every map's result.

ConvertWithMapsResponse.description: What a conversion with maps created.

channel.description:
G2-T1: the `channel` choice the request came through (`portal` for
an anonymous web form); unset leaves it empty.

request_type.description:
`project_request | change_request | issue_report | it_request |
hr_request | access_request | custom` — the same `service_work_request
.request_type` choice set. Not derived from the offering: an offering
can plausibly back more than one request type, so the caller states
it explicitly, the same "don't guess a product decision" reasoning
`convert.rs`'s required parent lookups already apply.

requester_id.description:
The `user_account` this request is filed on behalf of — the
caller's choice, made explicit, same reasoning as `convert.rs`'s
`project_id`/`organization_id` fields.

converted.description:
G2-T3: the records the request became at once, through the
offering's direct-creation conversion maps; empty when it has none
(or the conversion could not be made, which leaves the request to
convert by hand).

open_requests.description:
G2-T2: the requester's other open requests, newest first, so the
submission can be added to one instead. Empty when the caller may not
read work requests.

portal_token.description:
The self-service portal bearer token (`{public_id}.{secret}`) —
returned exactly once, here. Only its argon2 hash is persisted
(`service_work_request.portal_secret_hash`); this response is the only
place the raw secret ever exists.

reference.description:
G2-T2: the request's reference (`REQ-2026-00042`), when the
deployment's reference rule numbered it.

stopped_at_budget.description: Whether the time budget ended the improvement early.

commander_id.description: The commander; the caller when absent.

public.description: Show it on the public status page (default true).

status_title.description: The status page title; the ticket's subject when absent.

paged.description: The people paged now (none when already declared).

device_id.description: The device's id, as the asset's `device_id` holds it.

read_at.description: When the device read it; now when absent.

error.description: Why none was: `unknown_device`, `invalid` or the write's error.

reading_id.description: The reading record made, when one was.

DeviceReadingsIn.description: Readings a device posts, up to 500.

DeviceReadingsResult.description: Each posted reading's result, in order.

status.description:
`done` (acted now), `already_done`, `not_ready`, `busy` (another
call holds the line) or `failed`.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

sequence.description: Position in the technician's route, 1 first.

travel_minutes.description: Travel to this visit, in minutes (0 when not known).

note.description: What the agent should do next.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

message.description: The last status update; a standard text when absent.

MovementRecorded.description: A recorded movement and the balance after it.

reference.description: What caused it (an order, a work order line, a count).

NewTicketHandoff.description: A person's hand-off of a ticket.

OpenRequest.description: One of the requester's open requests, offered when they submit another.

OrderItemView.description: One item of an order, as its owner sees it.

PaginatedResponse_CatalogOffering.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_Handoff.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_InboxConversation.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description: One conversation: the record a mailbox's messages were routed to.

messages.description: Messages routed to it from this mailbox.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_InboxMailbox.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_OrderView.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description: One order, as its owner sees it.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_QueueOffer.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description: An offer of a queue item to an agent.

record_entity.description: The entity of the record the item holds (J10-T2 opens it).

record_id.description: The id of the record the item holds.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_TimelineEntry.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description: One entry in a record's timeline.

actor.description: B1-T1: who acted — the user, or the user an agent or flow acted for.

actor_kind.description: B1-T1: what kind of actor made the entry.

detail.description:
Kind-specific detail (audit operation and readable changed fields,
communication subject/channel, note title, activity type, decision
status, approval action and status, flow name, agent actions, …). A
JSON object rather than one struct with mostly-empty fields across
unrelated shapes.

pinned.description: B1-T2: pinned on this record, shown above the rest.

run_id.description: B1-T1: the agent session or flow instance, when the entry came from one.

source_entity.description:
The entity or ledger table the underlying row belongs to —
`audit_header`, `audit_detail` (state transitions),
`communication`, `note`, `activity`, `dashboard_decision`,
`approval_request`, `workflow_instance` or `agent_session`.

source_record.description:
B1-T1: the record the underlying row belongs to: this record, or a
related record rolled in.

summary.description: Short, human-readable description of the event.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

guide_id.description: An order guide whose offerings join the order with `guide_answers`.

title.description: The order's title; "Order of N items" when unset.

work_order_ids.description:
The work orders to plan; by default the day's scheduled work orders
with no technician.

QueueOffer.description: An offer of a queue item to an agent.

record_entity.description: The entity of the record the item holds (J10-T2 opens it).

record_id.description: The id of the record the item holds.

after.description: The previous page's `next_after`; omit for the first page.

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

SlaRecalculation.description: The outcome of recalculating one ticket's SLA.

recalculated.description:
`false` when the ticket's SLA was not unresolved (nothing to do), or
its policy no longer exists.

oneOf.description: The ticket's SLA status afterwards; `null` when no SLA was applied.

SourceRecord.description: B1-T1: the record an entry's row belongs to.

language.description: `en` (the default) or `ar`: the language of the emails.

StatusToken.description: A link's token (`?token=`, or the page's form field).

token.description: The signed token from the link.

SurveyForm.description: A survey as the respondent sees it.

questions.description: The questions: key, label, label_ar, type, required, options.

token.description: The signed token from the email.

TimelineEntryKind.description:
The source an entry came from. Entries sort by their wire name within one
timestamp, so the order is stable and documented: `activity`,
`agent_run`, `approval`, `audit_event`, `communication`, `decision`,
`flow_run`, `note`, `state_transition`, `web_visit`.

ToKind.description: Who a ticket is handed to.

UnresolvedReason.description:
Why a ticket's SLA has no deadline (D-517) — the value stored in
`service_ticket.sla_unresolved_reason`.

UnresolvedRecalculationSummary.description: A bounded page of unresolved-SLA recalculation.

next_after.description: Pass back as `after` for the next page; `null` when this was the last.

skipped.description:
Skipped because a concurrent pause/resume held the ticket's clock
lock; they stay unresolved and a later page run picks them up.

heartbeat_secs.description: Seconds until the next heartbeat is due.

viewers.description: Everyone else viewing the record now, most recent first.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

confirm.description: Must be `true`: the person has seen the preview.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
